title: Interpreting theories: translating domains and statements

based_on.title: When bi-interpretability implies synonymy
based_on.pages: Sections 2.1–2.2 and Appendix A.1–A.2 (elementary interpretation setup)

summary: Translate a theory into a definable part of another theory, preserving truth, proofs and consistency, and compose the translations.
abstract: A structure can contain a smaller world in which different mathematical statements make sense. A unary predicate can select its objects, formulas can describe its relations, and uniquely determined graphs can describe its functions. Quantifiers must then range over the selected objects. We construct this translation and prove that a statement is true in the smaller structure exactly when its translation is true in the original one. When the background theory proves that the selected domain is nonempty, the function graphs work, and the translated axioms hold, every theorem of the interpreted theory has a translated proof. This gives a direction of relative consistency and allows interpretations to be composed. Simple failures explain why domain nonemptiness and function closure are essential.
